title: Observer Channels Database Migrations And Session Ownership
summary: Distinguish current bounded HTTP and PostgreSQL operations from future bidirectional transport and deployment automation.

transport.current: Loopback HTTP request/response using cpp-httplib. Observer explicitly initiates authenticated metadata delivery, receipt confirmation and reconciliation. There is no implemented unsolicited Server event stream or remote execution channel.
transport.direction: A future Observer opens an authenticated outbound connection. Do not require an inbound developer-machine listener; remote traffic must use TLS with reviewed identity and authorization policy.
transport.candidate: WebSocket over TLS using an established asynchronous implementation such as Boost.Asio/Beast, with ordinary HTTP retained for bounded control/retrieval. This is a proposed transport candidate, not an installed dependency, completed benchmark or approved whole-service rewrite. SSE plus HTTP can be evaluated if only one-way notifications are actually needed.
transport.lifetime: Many connected Observers must not imply one blocked OS thread or one PostgreSQL lease per Observer. Event-loop callbacks dispatch bounded work; blocking database operations remain on bounded workers. Never hold a PostgreSQL connection while waiting for a client message, reconnect or acknowledgement.
transport.recovery: Heartbeat proves connectivity only. Sequence/cursor identity, durable outbox/ack, bounded queues, backpressure, reconnect and reconciliation provide delivery semantics. Notifications are invalidation hints until the durable authorized state is reread. No exactly-once network promise.
transport.authority: A channel grants no new filesystem, shell, source-export or publication authority. Typed operations need project/worktree/principal scope, request identity, limits and expiry. Server hints do not silently execute tests, publish indexes or apply project edits.

migrations.execution: The explicit command validates reviewed configuration and target database, acquires the exclusive lifecycle/migration fence, verifies applied ordered history/checksums, executes missing embedded SQL migrations and records their version/checksum in one PostgreSQL transaction. Ordinary serve/readiness never apply DDL. Development can invoke the command manually; SQL files are not pasted into a database by hand.
migrations.versioning: Current schema is 019. Source files 001..019 are immutable once applied; append the next migration. The current publication-history transition is owned by shin-publication-history-v1.json. The binary rejects unknown/newer/gapped/changed history and verifies physical schema. Server/Core/Observer release versions, database schema and wire versions are independent contracts.
migrations.roles: Use a separate schema-owner migrator credential. Runtime credentials are limited and do not migrate or rotate deployment identity. The current migrate command uses a reviewed service-config shape with migrator connection_file; deployment must provision its referenced paths/configuration explicitly.
migrations.deployment: A future CI/CD migration step or Kubernetes Job runs once under the existing database fence, not independently on every replica. This deployment automation is not implemented by this document. Stop/fence existing runtime sessions before migration: idle pooled connections also hold the shared lifecycle lock. Failed admission leaves the schema unchanged and the pipeline must not deploy incompatible workers.
migrations.rolling: Zero-downtime schema evolution is not currently certified. It needs separately designed expand/contract phases and compatible readers. Do not claim a rolling upgrade while requiring exact schema equality. Current migrations use transactional DDL; operations that cannot run in a transaction require a different explicit migration plan.
migrations.rollback: No automatic destructive down-migration. Use a reviewed forward repair or trusted backup/recovery procedure, preserving deployment identity rules. Updating the PostgreSQL server binary/major version is separate from application schema migration.
